# Coding stage assessment

## Evidence and baseline

- The complete pinned story requests a local Python 3.12 Flask, Jinja/server-rendered password-reset demonstration with pytest, synthetic accounts, a private in-memory notification sink, production-limitations documentation, and no deployment or new deployment workflows (`user_story`, characters 0-16000). The run-specific curated account recovery standard requires indistinguishable known/unknown request responses, at most five reset requests per account per hour, single-use links expiring 30 minutes after issuance, revocation of all active sessions on success, and owner notification (`knowledge`, `bcf198d8-a628-401c-8641-b726fcbd00b5`, `v1, chunk 0`).
- The attached 480 x 360 sign-in wireframe (`attachment`, `fd6b3020-ac35-442c-bd77-c53062c11e9c`, `sign-in-wireframe.png`) shows a white canvas, approximately centered thin dark outlined card (x about 70-410, y about 20-342), "Sign in" heading, "Email address" and "Password" labels, placeholders `name@example.com` and `********`, blue underlined "Forgot password?" link, dark rectangular "Sign in" button, and exact footer "No account? Contact your administrator." It proves neither actual masking nor sign-in authentication or recovery-page appearance.
- Approved `requirements_analysis`, `ui_analysis`, `solution_design`, and `test_case_design` stage outputs, plus the approved prospective risk register, were inspected via platform tools. The solution design enumerates TASK-001 through TASK-009 and maps REQ-001 through REQ-021; test design enumerates TC-001 through TC-026. These are specifications/proposed checks, not implemented features or passing results. The design deliberately excludes authentication behavior for the depicted button and external delivery.
- Repository baseline at `0065943` contains only a brief README, approved SDLC documents and prior stage artifacts. There is no application package, dependency manifest/lock, tests, runtime pin, `.gitignore`, build or lint configuration, `.github/workflows/` directory, persistent storage, or hosting configuration. Working tree was clean. Python 3.12.3 and `uv` are available; `python3.12 -m pytest --version` currently fails with `No module named pytest`. Do not interpret the absent dependency as a failing project test. No product files were modified during assessment.

## Implementation readiness and coverage

The approved design is feasible as a single-process Flask application: application factory with injectable UTC clock, hasher, CSPRNG token factory, fresh lock-protected in-memory state and private sink; thin browser routes render S1-S6 and delegate to a recovery service. TASK-001 foundation must precede S1, issuance and session registry; issuance and S1 feed CSRF-protected request pages; issuance/request pages feed secret-free link/intents; the registry and link handling feed atomic reset completion; comprehensive pytest coverage and documentation follow. Preserve the run's suggested coding ledger keys T002/TASK-001, T003/TASK-002, T004/TASK-003, T005/TASK-006, T006/TASK-004, T007/TASK-005, T008/TASK-007, T009/TASK-008 and T010/TASK-009, with T001 scaffold and T011 closing artifacts.

The scaffold should establish reproducible local Python 3.12 dependencies and a passing minimal pytest case before feature tasks. Approved design gate: `python3.12 -m pytest` from repository root; it lists no existing build or lint gate. For approval planning, propose `python3.12 -m compileall -q <package>` as build check and a pinned locally installed lint/format checker (for example `python3.12 -m ruff check .` and `python3.12 -m ruff format --check .`) after the scaffold creates them. Do not claim these gates already exist. A lock file should be generated by the chosen package manager rather than manually assembled; initial dependency installation is part of the future approved scaffold task.

Tests should be traceable by TC ID and cover synthetic isolation and no public sink, server-rendered wireframe and accessibility, known/unknown/capped complete HTTP-response parity, fifth/sixth and trailing-hour boundary, normalized concurrent issuance, issuance/sink failure rollback, GET non-consumption, strict issuance-based 30-minute deadline, replay/CSRF/intent isolation, all-or-nothing reset and simultaneous completion, revocation of multiple owner sessions, exact owner-addressed in-memory notices and no outbound calls. `tests.json` must enumerate all TC-001 through TC-026 with real automated references or an explicit manual reason. Browser interaction/visual assertions require an actual browser harness if claimed as automated; a Flask-client markup test alone cannot establish pixel geometry, typed-character visual masking or keyboard navigation. TC-025 needs a complete action record; TC-026 needs final baseline-to-delivery diff and action review. Do not mark these verified before evidence exists.

## Principal risks and boundaries

- Preserve account non-enumeration for known, unknown and capped valid requests across redirect, body, headers, cookies and S3. Apply the five-link cap only to accepted known-account issuances in a serialized trailing-hour window; no invented unknown-account quota. Residual timing disclosure remains a documented risk.
- Raw bearer links belong only in the private sink and initial link URL; persist digests, never reveal secrets in templates, redirects, cookies or application logs. A short-lived server-held reset intent and CSRF protection must not extend the link's issuance deadline. Initial browser-history/HTTP risks require documentation.
- Concurrency and injected failures must not consume issuance slots or partially commit password replacement, link consumption, all-session revocation and owner notice. Use a process-local lock and explicit failure-safe state transition; distinguish this demonstration from cross-worker/durable transactions.
- Fixture-created revocable sessions are required for REQ-012 coverage; neither a public test route nor a fabricated sign-in authentication flow is approved. The notification sink records events, not actual owner delivery.
- README must clearly describe restart loss, no shared rate/session state, no real delivery, local-only HTTP/cookie limitations and production prerequisites. No deployment, deployment scripts, hosting infrastructure or `.github/workflows/` edits are in scope; compare final changes to this baseline and review the action record separately.

No external service or Docker engine is required for the approved local-only design. Open questions about real sign-in authentication, actual link delivery, production password policy and hosting remain outside this stage's approved behavior; mainstream implementation details left open by the design can be recorded as decisions in the later approved plan/execution. This assessment is not an execution plan and makes no claim that any application test has passed.
